newsitem.title: USA: RightChoice sees premium growth up 7-9 pct.
newsitem.headline: RightChoice sees premium growth up 7-9 pct.

text.p: RightChoice Managed Care Inc said Wednesday that premium levels are targeted to increase 7 to 9 percent as of January 1997, when more of its underwritten members are eligible to re-enroll.
RightChoice also said it is targeting 8 to 10 percent growth in overall underwritten enrollment for 1997.
Included in this is new business expected from new preferred provider organization offerings in Illinois and health maintenance organization offerings in Missouri, RightChoice said.
The company, a publicly held subsidiary of Blue Cross and Blue Sheild of Missouri, said it also expects $1.4 million more in relocation expenses in the fourth quarter.

Corporate initiatives will cost about $3 million in the fourth quarter and $6 to $7 million in 1997, RightChoice said. It said it also expects a depreciation expense of about $5 to $6 million in 1997.
"Taking these factors in combination, we believe we are well-positioned to achieve 1997 growth targets," the company said in a release.
On Wednesday, RightChoice reported a third-quarter loss of $0.42 per share, including non-recurring charges, down from a $0.19 per share profit in the year-ago quarter.
